title: Unblock the shipping-quote API
problem: shipping.py serves shipping quotes. Both endpoints are async def, but they call carrier_quote, a blocking function from a sync-only SDK, directly. Under load, one slow carrier call freezes every request. Fix both endpoints so the blocking call never runs on the event loop's thread, while the async exchange_rate call is still awaited.
requirements: GET /quote/{country} returns {"country": ..., "eur": price}, or 404 if carrier_quote returns None
GET /quote/{country}/{currency} returns the price converted with exchange_rate, rounded to 2 decimals, under the lowercased currency key, or 404
carrier_quote never runs on the event loop's thread
Two requests can be in carrier_quote at the same time
exchange_rate is still awaited (it is async); don't change carrier_quote, exchange_rate or RATES
expectedBehavior: GET /quote/US/USD returns {"country": "US", "usd": 27.5}. Two concurrent requests whose carrier calls each wait for the other both succeed (the starter fails one with a 500 after 1 s).
edgeCases: An endpoint that needs both a blocking call and an await
The tests call carrier_quote through the module (they replace it with a fake), so look it up by name at call time
hints: Conceptual: FastAPI calls async def endpoints directly on the event loop, so a blocking call inside one blocks every request. It runs plain def endpoints in a threadpool.
Specific: an endpoint that only does blocking work can simply become def. An endpoint that must also await something has to stay async def, so move just the blocking call to a thread.
Implementation: change `async def quote` to `def quote`. In quote_in, replace the direct call with `price = await asyncio.to_thread(carrier_quote, country)`.
evaluation: No blocking call left directly inside an async def endpoint
The learner can explain which endpoint got which fix and why
